questions.text: Consider a singly linked list of the form where F is a pointer to the first element in the linked list and L is the pointer to the last element in the list. The time of which of the following operations depends on the length of the list?
questions.solution:
Deleting the last node requires updating the next pointer of the node before it, and finding that node means walking from F through the whole list. The other operations use F or L directly in constant time.

Answer: Delete the last element of the list

Delete the first element of the list
Add an element after the last element of the list
Interchange the first two elements of the list

questions.text: Given a binary-max heap. The elements are stored in an arrays as 25,14,16,13,10,8,12. What is the content of the array after two delete operations?
questions.solution:
Delete 1: move the last element 12 to the root [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [12, 14, 16, 13, 10, 8], sift down (swap with 16) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [16, 14, 12, 13, 10, 8].
Delete 2: move 8 to the root [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [8, 14, 12, 13, 10], sift down (swap with 14, then with 13) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [14, 13, 12, 8, 10].

Answer: 14,13,12,8,10

questions.text:
A hash table with 10 buckets with one slot pet per bucket is depicted here. The symbols, S1 to S7 are initially entered using a hashing function with linear probing. The maximum number of comparisons needed in searching an item that is not present is:
[latex]\begin{array}{|c|c|} \hline 0 & S 7 \\ \hline 1 & S 1 \\ \hline 2 & \\ \hline 3 & S 4 \\ \hline 4 & S 2 \\ \hline 5 & \\ \hline 6 & S 5 \\ \hline 7 & \\ \hline 8 & S 6 \\ \hline 9 & S 3 \\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]
questions.solution:
An unsuccessful search probes until it finds an empty slot. The longest run is from slot 8: slots 8, 9, 0, 1 are full and slot 2 is empty [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5 comparisons.

Answer: 5

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

This is the juggling (cycle) method of rotating left by k. Each cycle starts at i and moves elements forward by k positions (mod n) until it returns to the start:
- outer loop while i [latex]\lt[/latex] min (cycles start at indices below the smallest visited)
- inner loop while j != (n + i [latex]-[/latex] k) mod n
- A[j] = A[(j + k) mod n], then the saved temp goes to position (n + i [latex]-[/latex] k) mod n, and i = i + 1

Answer: Option 4
